deep.reconstruction:
This page is from the fair copy of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (1854; published posthumously by Dedekind in 1867). It closes the historical Section 3 and opens Section 4. There are no formulas or derivations on the page.

(a) End of the critique of Bessel. Bessel's changes to Dirichlet's proof (Astron. Nachr. No. 374) bring no real simplification of the reasoning. At most they put the proof into more familiar concepts, and its rigour and generality suffer considerably.

(b) State of the question. Whether a function f on [-π, π] can be represented as a(0)/2 + Σ (a_n cos nx + b_n sin nx) has so far been settled only under two hypotheses:
- (i) f is integrable throughout ('durchgehends eine Integration zulässt');
- (ii) f has only finitely many maxima and minima. These are Dirichlet's 1829 conditions, piecewise monotonicity plus integrability.

Riemann then explains why each hypothesis matters.
- If (ii) is dropped, Dirichlet's two integral theorems no longer suffice. These are the limits of ∫_0^h f(x) sin(kx)/sin(x) dx as k→∞, used to evaluate the Dirichlet-kernel partial sums.
- If (i) is dropped, even the Fourier determination of the coefficients, a_n = (1/π)∫ f(x) cos(nx) dx and b_n = (1/π)∫ f(x) sin(nx) dx, cannot be applied.

Hence the route Riemann takes in what follows, where the question is to be studied without special assumptions on f, is forced by this situation. A route as direct as Dirichlet's is impossible by the nature of the matter. (Implicitly, and this is my gloss: he will work with the series itself, via the twice-integrated series F(x) = C + C'x + A_0 x^2/2 - Σ A_n/n^2, rather than starting from the coefficient integrals.)

(c) Heading: 'Über den Begriff eines bestimmten Integrals und den Umfang seiner Gültigkeit. 4.' The remaining uncertainty in some fundamental points of the theory of definite integrals forces him to say something first about the concept of the definite integral and the scope of its validity. This announces the Riemann-sum definition of ∫_a^b f(x) dx given on the next page.
errors: No mathematical errors. The page contains only historical and methodological statements, and they are accurate.

Mild imprecision: Dirichlet (1829) also allowed finitely many points where f becomes infinite, provided the function remains integrable. Riemann's summary 'durchgehends eine Integration zulässt' covers this loosely. This is not an error.

results.what: Summary that Fourier-series representability was known only for integrable functions with finitely many maxima and minima (Dirichlet conditions). Dropping finiteness of extrema defeats Dirichlet's integral theorems; dropping integrability defeats the Fourier coefficient formulas.
results.modern_name: Dirichlet conditions for convergence of Fourier series; motivation for Riemann's general theory of trigonometric series
results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet (1829) for the conditions; Riemann (1854, publ. 1867) for this critique

results.what: Methodological claim that a general theory must avoid Dirichlet's direct approach and proceed from the series itself rather than from the coefficient integrals.
results.modern_name: Riemann's approach to trigonometric series (Riemann's first and second lemmas, formal double integration)

results.what: Announcement of Section 4 on the concept of the definite integral.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the well-known Habilitationsschrift on trigonometric series, published by Dedekind in 1867. Its text matches the published version: the end of the historical §3 and the heading of §4 on the Riemann integral. Nothing here is new or uncredited.

checkable.asserts: A continuous function can have infinitely many maxima and minima near a point (x*sin(1/x), extended by 0). Such functions fall outside Dirichlet's hypothesis (ii).
The Fourier coefficient formula b_n=(1/pi)∫ f sin(nx) dx works for an integrable f (here f=x), giving b_n=2(-1)^(n+1)/n. Riemann notes this formula is unavailable when f is not integrable.
Model of Dirichlet's integral theorem: ∫_0^∞ sin(kx)/x dx = π/2. This is the type of limit Dirichlet's proof relies on.

transcription_corrections: The first word 'drungen' is the end of a word hyphenated from the previous page ('Ab-'). The published text reads 'Abänderungen'; the copy appears to have 'Ab-[än]drungen'.
A small superscript '14' stands above the line near 'hierdurch, wie' at the right margin. It is likely a marginal page or folio marker (corresponding to the folio number 14r), not part of the text.
The folio/page number '19.' at top right is omitted in the machine transcription.
The section heading 'Ueber den Begriff eines bestimmten Integrals und den Umfang seiner Gültigkeit.' is centred above the numeral '4.', which the transcription renders correctly.
